title: Iraq coach asks FIFA to delay World Cup play-off game due to Middle East conflict
content:
Graham Arnold, head coach of Iraq’s soccer team, has asked FIFA to reschedule the nation’s World Cup play-off game due to travel issues stemming from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

Iraq is set to play the winner of Bolivia vs Suriname in the inter-confederation play-offs, with the victor of that game claiming one of the final two spots at this summer’s World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

The play-off game is scheduled to take place on March 31 in Monterrey, Mexico at Estadio BBVA. Bolivia and Suriname are set to play on March 26 at the same stadium.

Iraq, along with several other Middle Eastern countries, closed its airspace following military attacks by the U.S. and Israel on Iran, which borders Iraq.

On March 3, Iraq said that Arnold was unable to leave the United Arab Emirates because of airspace closures and that several staff members and players were unable to secure visas for Mexico as embassies remained closed.

In a statement provided to the Australian Associated Press, Arnold explained that, as things stand, members of team would be unable to travel for the game and suggested that it should be rescheduled.

“In my opinion, if FIFA were to delay the game, it gives us time to prepare properly,” Arnold said. “Let Bolivia play Suriname this month and then a week before the World Cup, we play the winner in the United States. The winner of that game stays on and the loser goes home.”

Iraq remains scheduled to play in their qualifying match on March 31. The Athletic has contacted FIFA for comment.

Arnold also suggested that Iraq would replace Iran at the tournament if Iran did not compete, though any potential replacement has not yet been officially confirmed.

“It also gives FIFA more time to decide what Iran is going to do,” he said. “If Iran withdraws, we go into the World Cup and it gives the UAE, who we beat in qualifying, the chance to prepare for either Bolivia or Suriname.

“A team made up only of players from outside Iraq would not be our best team, and we need our best team available for the country’s biggest game in 40 years.

“Our federation’s president Adnan Dirjal is working around the clock trying to plan and prepare to make everyone in Iraq’s dream come true, so we need this decision to be made quickly.

“The Iraqi people are so passionate about the game of football that it is insane. The fact that they haven’t qualified for 40 years is probably the main reason I took this job.”

Arnold, who is from Sydney and twice managed the Australian national team, is aiming to lead Iraq to its second-ever World Cup and first since 1986. Iraq lost each of its group-stage games at that tournament, against Paraguay, Belgium and Mexico.

Iraq earned one of the six places at the inter-confederation play-offs by beating the UAE in the final round of Asian qualifying. As one of the two highest-seeded teams in the play-offs according to FIFA rankings, Iraq only needs to win one game to qualify.

On the other side of the play-offs, New Caledonia will play Jamaica on March 26 in Zapopan, Mexico, with the winner playing DR Congo five days later for the other World Cup spot.
